To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ET through subwavelength holes is caused by a resonance of the electric field around the holes, and that the onset of the resonance is related with the excitation of higher-order modes of the screen.
the onset of extraordinary transmission is associated with the continuous increase of the electric energy around the hole as the frequency approaches some of the higher resonant modes of the screen.

the onset of ET is associated with the continuous increase of electric energy around the apertures as the frequency approaches some of the higher modes associated with the grating periodicity and the fact that the role of surface waves -spoof plasmons- is to provide the required coupling between the incident wave and these higher-order modes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analytical study of the transmission coefficient of electromagnetic waves through metallic screens perforated with holes of subwavelength diameter, in a simple canonical example.
the study of the extraordinary transmission of electromagnetic waves in metallic screens perforated with holes.
the analytical solution of a canonical case of extraordinary transmission through a metallic diffraction screen with small holes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenomenon is a combination of two effects: the continuous growth of the excess electric energy around holes as the frequency increases and the excitation of surface plasmons.
the phenomenon of extraordinary transmission through subwavelength apertures is a consequence of the continuous accumulation of excess electromagnetic energy around the holes.
the phenomenon of ET is a consequence of the excitation of a large number of higher-order modes in the screen, whose contribution to the total field is enhanced by the presence of a surface wave.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phenomenon of extraordinary transmission can be understood from an analytical point-of-view as the result of the continuous accumulation of excess energy in the near field of the screen, which is enhanced by the existence of surface modes.
ET is the result of the interplay between the excitation of surface waves and the excitation of the higher-order diffraction modes of the screen.
the extraordinary transmission of electromagnetic waves is not a mere consequence of diffraction effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ET effect is not an intrinsic property of the holes, but rather a consequence of the periodicity of a screen perforated with subwavelength holes.

the transmission coefficient of a metallic screen perforated by subwavelength holes is a function of two independent parameters: the size of the holes, and the distance between the holes and the screen.

, although ET can be described by a simple closed-form expression, its occurrence is not a trivial effect, but a consequence of a delicate interplay of several factors, including the excitation of surface modes, the excitation of higher-order modes, and the excitation of evanescent waves.
